acceptance: Each listed platform either has stub-verified run-timeout cleanup or a recorded owner decision to leave it without.
context: Filed 2026-11-25 at the close of the run-timeout effort (umbrella run-timeout-plan-20261120, done). Evidence read that day; re-read code, docs and run folders before acting.
description:
## Problem
These platforms still show the no-cleanup warning at the run limit (#4507, docs/operations/run-safety.md (capability table)), each for a recorded reason that may have a workaround:
- Snowflake: the connector sets the query id only after a synchronous statement returns. Possible route: `cursor.execute_async` / `sfqid` returns the id at submission, then `SYSTEM$CANCEL_QUERY` or `cursor.abort_query`.
- ClickHouse Cloud: ids are generated by the run, but `KILL QUERY` acts on one replica and a finished statement can raise `NOTHING_TO_KILL`. Possible route: `KILL QUERY ON CLUSTER default WHERE query_id = ...` with `NOTHING_TO_KILL` tolerated, over a second connection.
- Databricks DataFrame and Snowpark Connect: session interrupt needs operation tags the adapters do not set. Possible route: tag each operation at submission and interrupt by tag.
Redshift, Firebolt, Databend and MotherDuck have no cancel on the connector path; out of scope unless that changes.

## Change
For each platform the owner picks, implement cleanup with the existing hook and pattern, set the manifest capability `run_timeout_cleanup`, and update the table; for the rest keep the recorded reason.

## Decision gates
- STOP and ask the owner (choice dialog) which platforms to implement, with the route and its risk for each (Snowflake async execution changes how queries are timed: check it does not move work into or out of the query timer).
- Never put a deadline check inside a query timer; no new default timeout.
- Only stop what this run started.

## Verification rubric
Pass: per implemented platform, stubbed-client tests (started work cancelled, pre-existing not, failure reported with exit 124 kept) that fail before; query timings unchanged on the timing-contract tests; `make platform-manifest-check` and `make pr-preflight` exit 0; table updated.
Fail: a timing change, or cleanup that could stop work the run did not start.

## Guardrails
Work in a linked worktree (`make worktree-create`), never the primary clone. Edit files with the edit tool, never by script. Heavy work (benchmarks, test tiers, UAT, generators at scale) only through `make heavy-run` or lock-taking entry points; never skip the lock, admission or watchdog; never delete anything under `~/Developer/benchmark_runs`. No live cloud run and no cloud credentials unless this item's Decision gates say the owner approved it in the current task. BenchBox imposes no default run limit: add none. No comments or docstrings in first-party code; one changelog fragment for a user-facing change. Never post a stand-in review, close and reopen a pull request to restart CI, use `--no-verify`, force-push, or rewrite an author. Arm once; a second time only after fixing the cause the refusal named. Reply on every review thread; resolve it only after the bot's review of the new head does not raise it again.
